title: How do volcanoes erupt?
examples: What is the difference between magma and lava?
Do all volcanoes erupt the same way?
Why are volcanoes usually found near plate boundaries?

explain.say: Today we are learning about volcanoes and how they erupt.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: inside a volcano. Look at the ash cloud, the crater and the lava flow. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Deep underground, there is hot, melted rock called magma.
As magma builds up, the gas trapped inside creates great pressure.
The Earth's plates are large pieces of the Earth's crust.
When plates meet, magma can force its way up through cracks.
Volcanoes can be shield, composite, or cinder cone shapes.

faq.q: Does magma turn into lava when it comes out?
faq.a: Yes, when magma reaches the surface, it is called lava. Magma is underground, and lava is on the surface.
asks: What is the difference between magma and lava?

faq.q: Are volcanoes always near plate edges?
faq.a: Most volcanoes do form where tectonic plates are moving past each other. This movement creates the openings for magma.
asks: Why are volcanoes found near plate boundaries?

faq.q: What causes the pressure inside the magma?
faq.a: The pressure comes from gases trapped within the hot, melted rock. These gases need a way to escape.
asks: Why does magma build up pressure?

faq.q: Are all volcanoes the same shape?
faq.a: No, volcanoes can take different shapes depending on what they are made of. They can be shield, cone, or cinder.
asks: What are the types of volcanoes?

faq.q: Is magma always hotter than lava?
faq.a: Magma is generally hotter because it has been deep underground. Lava cools down quickly once it reaches the air.
asks: Which is hotter, magma or lava?

facts: Magma is molten rock found beneath the Earth's surface.
Pressure builds up inside magma from dissolved gases.
Tectonic plates are huge sections of the Earth's crust.
When magma reaches the surface, it is called lava.

quiz.say: Melted rock found underground is called:
quiz.why: Magma is the term used for rock that is still beneath the Earth's surface.

wrong.1: Lava is what you see after the rock has come out.
wrong.2: Pressure is the force that pushes the rock up.
wrong.3: A plate is a large piece of the Earth's outer shell.

quiz.say: What causes the pressure that pushes magma up?
quiz.why: The gases trapped inside the hot rock expand, creating the force needed for eruption.

wrong.0: Cooling rock would reduce pressure, not build it up.
wrong.1: Gravity pulls things down, it does not push magma up.
wrong.3: Plate movement helps open the way, but the gas creates the push.

quiz.say: If a volcano is very wide with gentle slopes, it is most likely a:
quiz.why: Shield volcanoes build up with many thin, runny layers of lava, making them broad.

wrong.0: Volcanoes always have a noticeable mound shape.
wrong.2: Composite volcanoes are built up with many different, hard layers.
wrong.3: Cinder cones are usually small and steep piles of loose rock.
